description: The tools and theory for finding bugs and proving their absence: dataflow analysis, abstract interpretation, symbolic execution, software model checking, fuzzing, human review and deductive proof. Students write small analysers, run symbolic and fuzzing tools on real-style programs, and prove selected functions correct.
modelledOn: Nielson, Nielson and Hankin, Principles of Program Analysis
Moller and Schwartzbach, Static Program Analysis
Ammann and Offutt, Introduction to Software Testing
outcomes: Explain soundness, completeness and the limits set by undecidability, and classify analyses by the guarantees they give.
Implement dataflow analyses with the worklist algorithm over a control-flow graph and prove that they terminate.
Design an abstract domain, apply widening, and argue the soundness of an abstract interpreter for a small language.
Use symbolic execution, bounded model checking and fuzzing to find and reproduce defects, and interpret their counterexamples.
Plan and run a code review or inspection, and combine reviews, tools and testing into a verification strategy for a given risk level.
Specify and prove a small program correct with contracts and invariants using a deductive verifier.

units.title: Foundations of program analysis
topics: Static versus dynamic analysis; soundness, completeness, false positives and false negatives
Undecidability of semantic properties (Rice's theorem) and why analyses approximate
Representations: abstract syntax trees, control-flow graphs, call graphs and static single assignment form
A small imperative language and its operational semantics for analysis
Bug classes worth analysing: null dereference, overflow, injection, resource leaks and races

units.title: Dataflow analysis
topics: Lattices, monotone transfer functions and the fixed-point theorem
Reaching definitions, live variables and available expressions
The worklist algorithm, ordering and complexity
Constant propagation and its non-distributive nature
Interprocedural analysis: call graphs, context sensitivity and summaries
Pointer and alias analysis: Steensgaard and Andersen styles
Taint analysis for security: sources, sinks and sanitisers

units.title: Abstract interpretation
topics: Concrete and abstract semantics; Galois connections and soundness
Non-relational domains: signs, parity and intervals
Widening and narrowing for loops
Relational domains: octagons and polyhedra; cost versus precision
Building a sound abstract interpreter for a small language and proving its key lemmas
Industrial analysers: absence of runtime errors, alarms triage and tuning precision

units.title: Symbolic execution
topics: Symbolic states, path conditions and forking at branches
Constraint solving with SMT solvers: bit-vectors, arrays and integers
Path explosion and mitigation: search heuristics, state merging and summaries
Concolic execution: concrete runs guiding symbolic exploration
Modelling memory, pointers, loops and the environment; floating point and its difficulties
Applications: test generation, exploit finding, equivalence checking and regression analysis

units.title: Model checking software
topics: From programs to transition systems; state-space explosion in software
Predicate abstraction and counterexample-guided abstraction refinement
Bounded model checking of C-like programs: loop unwinding, assertions and SAT/SMT encodings
Concurrency: interleavings, data races, lockset and happens-before analysis
Checking protocols and device drivers; interpreting counterexample traces

units.title: Fuzzing and property-based testing
topics: Property-based testing: generators, properties and shrinking
Random and mutation-based fuzzing; coverage-guided fuzzing with feedback
Grammar-based and structure-aware fuzzing for parsers and protocols
Sanitizers and runtime checkers for memory and undefined behaviour
Test oracles and metamorphic testing
Mutation testing and coverage criteria as measures of test strength
Fuzzing in continuous integration; triage, deduplication and reporting of crashes

units.title: Reviews and inspections
topics: Formal inspection: roles, preparation, inspection rate and exit criteria
Modern code review: tool support, review size, turnaround and effectiveness evidence
Reading techniques and checklists: perspective-based and security-focused reviews
Human factors in review: bias, fatigue and psychological safety
Combining reviews with static analysis in the pipeline; review metrics and their limits

units.title: Proof of program correctness
topics: Specification with contracts: preconditions, postconditions, frame conditions and ghost code
Verification-condition generation and automated provers
Loop invariants and variants in a deductive verifier
Separation logic and heap-manipulating programs
Interactive proof assistants for software and what verified systems have achieved
Assurance cases and choosing among techniques by risk, cost and criticality
Project: verify or analyse a chosen module and report on the evidence

schedule.title: Foundations: soundness, limits and representations
schedule.exercise: Classify five tools by their soundness and completeness claims, sketch why a perfect null-pointer checker cannot exist, and draw the control-flow graph of a loop with a break.

tasks.title: Build the control-flow graph of a given function with a loop and a conditional, and label basic blocks and edges
Convert a straight-line program with branches into static single assignment form with phi functions, and check semantic equivalence by running both
Write a small checker that flags use of a variable before assignment across branches, and test it on 10 programs with known results

schedule.title: Classical dataflow analyses
schedule.exercise: Compute reaching definitions and live variables for a program with a loop by iterating to a fixed point, and show why the lattice height bounds the iterations.

tasks.title: Iterate live-variable analysis on a control-flow graph by hand, showing the in and out sets of every block until the fixed point
Implement a generic worklist solver and instantiate it for reaching definitions and available expressions on 5 test graphs
Implement constant propagation, show a program where merging at a join loses precision, and compare with a path-sensitive result

schedule.title: Interprocedural, pointer and taint analysis
schedule.exercise: Build a call graph for a small program, compute points-to sets by the Andersen method, and list the taint flows from user input to a database query.

tasks.title: Build a call graph with virtual calls resolved by class hierarchy, and mark which edges are imprecise
Implement Andersen-style points-to analysis with constraint propagation for 20 statements, and compare it with the unification-based result
Write a taint analysis that finds flows from request parameters to query calls through assignments and calls, and test it with and without sanitisers

schedule.title: Abstract domains and soundness
schedule.exercise: Define the concrete and abstract semantics for sign analysis, show the abstraction and concretisation maps form a Galois connection, and analyse a short program by hand.

tasks.title: Define a sign domain with join and abstract addition and multiplication, and prove soundness of the abstract addition on all cases
Implement an interval domain with abstract arithmetic and use it to analyse straight-line programs, checking results against concrete runs
Analyse a loop with intervals in the visualiser, watching the bounds climb, then apply widening and narrowing and compare the final invariants

schedule.title: Relational domains and building an analyser
schedule.exercise: Show an assertion that intervals cannot prove but octagons can, and build an interval analyser for a small imperative language that reports possible division by zero.

tasks.title: Represent the constraints of a program state as an octagon, take a join, and show a relational fact lost by intervals
Build an abstract interpreter with intervals and widening for a while-language, and report array-bound and division-by-zero alarms for 8 programs
Triage 20 alarms from an analyser into true bugs and false positives, find their causes, and tune the domain to remove half the false ones

schedule.title: Symbolic execution basics
schedule.exercise: Symbolically execute a function with three branches, write the path conditions, solve them with an SMT solver, and list the test inputs that cover every path.

tasks.title: Step a symbolic executor through a function with two branches, tracking symbolic state and path conditions, and list reachable paths
Solve the path conditions of a function with the SMT solver and produce a concrete test input for each feasible path
Run symbolic exploration on a program with a loop over symbolic input, count paths at several bounds, and test search heuristics for coverage

schedule.title: Concolic testing and applications
schedule.exercise: Run a concolic execution loop by hand on a program with a hash check, and explain which program features defeat symbolic execution.

tasks.title: Implement a small concolic loop that runs the program, negates the last branch condition, solves, and repeats until all paths are covered
Model symbolic memory with arrays for a program that indexes a buffer, and find the input that causes an out-of-bounds write
Use symbolic execution to check that two versions of a function are equivalent, and produce a distinguishing input for a buggy refactoring

schedule.title: Software model checking
schedule.exercise: Run bounded model checking on a C-like program with an off-by-one bug, read the counterexample trace, and explain how predicate abstraction and refinement would prove a lock protocol correct.

tasks.title: Check an assertion in a C program with bounded model checking at unwind bounds 2, 4 and 8, and read the counterexample trace
Walk through abstraction and refinement of a lock-usage program, showing each spurious counterexample and the predicate added to remove it
Find the data race in a two-thread counter program by exploring interleavings, then fix it with a lock and recheck for races

schedule.title: Property-based testing and fuzzing
schedule.exercise: Write properties for a sorting function and a parser, shrink a failing case to a minimal one, and fuzz a small file-format parser for crashes.

tasks.title: Write property-based tests for a sort function, find the bug in a faulty version, and shrink the failing input to the smallest example
Build a mutation-based fuzzer with coverage feedback for a toy parser, and compare crashes found against pure random inputs in 10,000 runs
Write a grammar-based generator for a small expression language and use it to find crashes in an evaluator that random bytes miss

schedule.title: Oracles, mutation testing and fuzzing in practice
schedule.exercise: Define metamorphic relations for a routing function, measure a test suite with mutation score, and set up a fuzzing job that triages and deduplicates crashes.

tasks.title: Write metamorphic tests for a route-length function, such as symmetry and triangle inequality, and catch two injected bugs
Mutate a function with 20 mutation operators, run its test suite, compute the mutation score, and add tests to kill the survivors
Deduplicate 200 fuzzer crashes by stack signature, rank the unique ones by exploitability, and write a clear report for the top one

schedule.title: Reviews and inspections
schedule.exercise: Run a structured inspection on a short module with defect log and rates, then compare what review found with what a static analyser and a test suite found.

tasks.title: Conduct a formal inspection in a case file with assigned roles, log defects found at a given inspection rate, and decide the exit outcome
Review a pull request for a payment function using a security checklist, list the defects found, and rank them by severity in the case file
Analyse review data for 100 changes, relate review size to defects found with a plot and regression, and recommend a maximum change size

schedule.title: Contracts and deductive verification
schedule.exercise: Write contracts for a bounded stack and a binary search, generate the verification conditions, and discharge them with a prover or by hand.

tasks.title: Write preconditions, postconditions and a class invariant for a bounded stack, and check them with runtime assertions on random operation sequences
Annotate a binary search with an invariant and variant in a deductive verifier, and fix the annotation when the verifier rejects it
Prove by hand the correctness of list reversal on a linked list in separation logic, using the points-to and separating conjunction notation

schedule.title: Choosing techniques and the verification project
schedule.exercise: Choose a combination of review, analysis, testing and proof for three systems of different criticality, and present your analysis or verification project and its evidence.

tasks.title: Choose verification techniques for a mobile-money ledger, a clinic scheduler and an infusion pump controller in a case file, and defend each plan
Compare the guarantees given by static analysis, bounded model checking and proof on the same function, tabulating what each can and cannot show
Verify a chosen module with at least two techniques, report bugs found, residual risk and the cost in effort for each technique
